params.body:
Fixes bevinding weigering-om-de-foto-is-geen-storing.

## What was wrong

remove.bg answers 400 for a photo it cannot cut out. One such answer ("Could not identify foreground") stopped being reported on 21 September 2026, recognised by matching that sentence in the exception message. Three days later the same monitoring issue reopened: the last occurrence is `failed_to_read_image`, a sibling answer about the image, filed under the same title because the error list groups on the message. Thirty occurrences in four days, five dealers, for photos the platform handled correctly.

Where the answer was recognised, the dealer was told nothing: a bulk run over thirty photos read as finished, and the three interior shots came back unchanged without a word.

## What changes

**One classifier, by remove.bg's own error code** (`App\Support\RemoveBgRefusal`). Read from their swagger.yaml, a closed list of the 400 codes that are about the image:

| code | shown as |
|---|---|
| `unknown_foreground` | no car recognised |
| `failed_to_read_image`, `invalid_file_type`, `invalid_dimensions`, `file_too_large`, `resolution_too_high` | photo not readable |

Everything else stays a reported fault with the existing "the image service returned no result" on the tile: 402 (credits), 403 (key), 429 (rate limit), 5xx, a parameter we sent wrong, and any code nobody has read yet. An image-level code under another status is a fault too. An answer without a code is still recognised by the sentence that was matched before.

**For an image-level refusal** (`Photo::old_remove_background`, the only call to `POST /removebg`):

- no `report()`; one `Log::info` with the photo id, the code and remove.bg's sentence;
- the upload (`path`) is never written; the original stands in as the cut-out, as R S1-6.8 already said, so the row records that the photo had its turn;
- an image we cannot make a thumbnail of either gets no stand-in and nothing is thrown, so the job is not retried (it has `tries = 10`, and every retry would be another call for the same answer);
- the job carries on: `processing` goes to 0, a platform copy still gets its plate blurred.

**What the dealer sees.** When the dealer asked for the background of an own photo (the wand or the bulk button), the tile says "Achtergrond niet verwijderd. Geen wagen herkend op deze foto." without "try again", and the end of a bulk run counts those photos apart, by their place in the grid, as a warning and not an error:

> Bij 3 foto's kon de achtergrond niet verwijderd worden (geen wagen herkend): foto 4, 7, 9. De foto's zelf zijn ongewijzigd.

Photos where the service really failed keep their own red notify. nl, fr, en, de.

A platform copy does not get the reason: a shared vehicle gets a copy of every photo, interiors included, and a chip on each of those would say "refused" about a copy that is exactly what it should be.

**Not asked again.** "All photos that still have a background" skips a refused photo (it has the stand-in, or its reason is noted). A photo the dealer selects by hand does go again. remove.bg charges no credits for a 400 (their spec: "no credits charged").

## Tests

- `APhotoWithoutAForegroundIsNotAFaultTest` was two assertions on the source text; it now runs the call with `Http::fake` and `Exceptions::fake`: each of the six image codes leaves the upload untouched, writes the stand-in, logs at info with the photo id and the code, and reports nothing; 402, 403, 429, 500, a parameter error, an unknown code and an image code under 402 are reported and leave no cut-out; an unreadable image does not throw.
- `OwnPhotoBackgroundTest`: in one bulk run the photo that ran out of credits is reported once and the interior is not; the interior is not sent a second time by the "all" mode, its tile carries the reason, a selection sends it again, restoring the original clears it; a platform copy without a car is finished without a reason on its tile; a success still works.

Rules: R S1-6.43 (new), R S1-6.8 points to it.
params.title: No foreground is an answer, not an error: remove.bg refusing the image is told to the dealer and no longer reported
